title: convergent-shadow-funnel-with-staged-ab-scheduler-and-rewind-playbook
author: Marina Kowalski
ci_checks: integration tests: flaky -> rerun -> passed (shadow-path tests)
perf-bench: passed (tail latency within SLO for 99th)
description:
Motivation:
As customers adopt mixed deployment strategies (canary + A/B + shadow), the orchestration layer must support convergent routing where multiple validation modes (shadow verification, staggered A/B slices, and canary traffic) cooperate and automatically trigger safe rewind/rollback when cross-signal regressions appear. This PR introduces the "Convergent Shadow Funnel" controller plus a staged A/B scheduler and an operational rewind playbook to reduce manual intervention during rollouts.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a Convergent Shadow Funnel controller that can consume multiple telemetry anchors (latency, top-k disagreement, hallucination rate, token-level perplexity) and compute a single safety score used by rollout policies.
- Implements a staged A/B scheduler that supports timeboxed slices, entropy seeding to avoid cohort bias, and deterministic replayable slice assignments for reproducible rollbacks/bisects.
- Introduces a Rewind Playbook subsystem: snapshot-backed checkpointing for rollout state, fast-rehearsal mode (replay captured traffic against candidate snapshots), and automated rollback steps with human-notify hooks.
- Extends telemetry schema to include per-cohort drift counters and a lightweight provenance header so promoted requests can be traced back through the funnel.
- Adds unit and integration tests for safety gate logic, and a simulation harness (pkg/simulator) to run stochastic rollouts offline.

Why this approach: 
- Many regressions are multi-signal (slight latency increase + falls in answer-value agreement). By fusing signals into a convergent safety score we reduce false positives while still surfacing compound failures.
- Deterministic slice assignment and snapshotting let us perform reproducible bisects and rehearse candidate rollbacks without touching production traffic.

Design highlights: 
- Safety score is a weighted composite (configurable via rollout policy). Default anchors: latency_p99, payload_disagreement_rate, hallucination_rate, generated_token_entropy_change. Each anchor has an independent threshold and burn-in period.
- The staged A/B scheduler supports progressive slice expansion: initial micro-slices (0.1% cohorts), warmup (1%), validation (5%), ramp (10-50%). Expansion is gated on the safety score and custom metric predicates.
- Shadow fusion accepts multiple model variants and performs lossy sampling for high-throughput workloads (configurable sampling ratio). Shadow traffic is mirrored asynchronously; result diffs are scored and fed back into the funnel.
- Rewind Playbook: on trigger, the controller creates a freeze snapshot (routing table + cohort mapping + model variant pointers), attempts a dry-run rehearse using captured sample traffic, then executes rollback with sticky session preservation. Hooks notify the on-call channel with automatic postmortem starters.

Checklist (what landed):
- [x] Controller: pkg/controller/convergent_funnel_controller.go
- [x] Scheduler: pkg/orchestrator/ab_scheduler.go
- [x] Snapshot & playbook: pkg/playbook/rewind_playbook.go + state snapshots in pkg/state
- [x] Telemetry: telemetry/schema/anchors.proto and telemetry/aggregator adapters
- [x] Simulation harness and smoke scenarios: pkg/simulator/*
- [x] Docs: docs/runbooks/rewind-playbook.md and docs/rollouts/convergent-funnel.md
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + simulation scenarios

Testing and validation notes: 
- Ran sim harness with 10k synthetic sessions for 50 random seeds; median safety false-positive < 1.2% for default thresholds.
- Staging deploy validated with a live shadow run across two canary cohorts; observed expected scoring behavior and deterministic replayable slices.
- Perf bench shows additional ~2% CPU overhead on routing path for mirrored requests when sampling ratio=1.0; recommended default sampling=0.25 for production.

Migration notes: 
- The rollout policy schema is backward compatible. New anchors are opt-in; existing policies keep previous behavior unless updated.
- Customers using custom rollout tooling that rely on raw mirror payloads may need to adapt to the new provenance header. Migration docs included.

Operational playbook (short):
1) If safety score crosses threshold, controller pauses expansion and emits an incident with snapshot ID.
2) Run "rw rehearse <snapshot-id>" in staging using captured traffic from the snapshot; compare safety score deltas.
3) If rehearsals confirm regression, run "rw rollback <snapshot-id> --preserve-sessions" which applies snapshot routing and backs out head pointers.
4) Post-rollback: schedule bisect using deterministic slice seed from snapshot metadata.

Related: ENG-3241 (convergent rollouts), PM-842 (telemetry anchors), SUP-1182 (customer incident that motivated deterministic replay).

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on safety score semantics and default weightings in config/defaults.go; weight choices are conservative but we should validate at scale.
- Scheduler expansion windows are intentionally conservative; we can tune based on telemetry after launch.
- Performance knobs for shadow sampling are in orchestration config; recommended production defaults are documented in docs/rollouts/convergent-funnel.md.

Require approvals from SRE and Reliability before merge.
